critic_risk_flags: Observation-target alignment is superficially strong (observe H for hospitalization rate), but explicit H dynamics (I→H rate and H duration) are likely weakly identifiable with only ~31 training weeks and a single season. This increases parameter tradeoffs and forecast instability relative to delayed_I, which is explicitly noted as plausible in the surveillance semantics.

Adds waning immunity (SEIRS) which is unlikely to be identifiable in a short single-season window and risks over-flexing tails/rebounds. For a high-peaked single-season hospitalization series, the extra degree of freedom is more likely to overfit than to capture a reliably estimable mechanism.
